Revised assessment: slightly negative overall, tempered by strong countercyclical policy support.

Supporting evidence from the statement
- Negative: “The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.” Also, “Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined,” and “the energy sector has come under stress.”
- Positive policy offset: “The Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 0 to 1/4 percent,” is “prepared to use its full range of tools,” and will purchase “at least $500 billion” in Treasuries and “at least $200 billion” in agency MBS to support market functioning and credit flow.

How the literature modifies the sentiment
- Countercyclical monetary policy dampens downturns: The monetary policy stance literature notes that countercyclical easing helps stabilize output and reduce fluctuations (monetary policy stance—countercyclical policy dampens fluctuations; monetary policy influences aggregate spending).
- Credit channel and external finance premium: Contractionary policy raises the external finance premium; by the same mechanism, the announced expansionary actions should lower financing spreads, supporting investment and especially small and inventory-intensive firms (credit markets—imperfect information; “Contractionary Monetary Policy INCREASES External Finance Premium”; Gertler and Gilchrist 1994; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994).
- Liquidity support at the zero lower bound: With the policy rate at 0–0.25% and swap lines/discount window/repo operations expanded, the Fed is addressing liquidity constraints and funding-market dysfunctions that can amplify recessions (Liquidity Buffers—liquidity effects; Discount Window; U.S. dollar liquidity swap arrangements; Federal Reserve Bank of New York operations).
- Expectations and inflation: With inflation running below 2% and market-based compensation declining, aggressive easing is consistent with the natural-rate/expectations-centric view (Friedman-Phelps; Svensson on inflation-forecast targeting), helping anchor longer-term expectations while supporting real activity.

Net effect
- The explicit recognition of severe near-term downside risks keeps the tone negative. However, the breadth and scale of rate cuts, QE, and liquidity facilities—consistent with the literature on countercyclical stabilization and credit channels—materially mitigate the negative outlook. Therefore, the sentiment is less negative than a reading focused only on the near-term shock.
